newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan electricity firms to raise July-Sept rates.
newsitem.headline: Japan electricity firms to raise July-Sept rates.

text.p: Most Japanese utilities will boost electricity rates in the July to September period compared to the previous quarter, reflecting higher fuel costs, an industry body said on Friday.
It will be the fifth consecutive quarter the utilities have raised their rates, and come despite growing government pressure on the utilities to slash their rates to comparable overseas levels.

The average household of four, which currently pays about 6,722 to 7,557 yen a month, will have to pay 14 to 68 yen more following the change by nine of Japan's 10 electricity utilities, the Federation of Electric Power Companies said.
The utilities based their calculations for their July-September rates on fuel procurement costs during the January-March period, the federation said.

Global crude and liquefied natural gas prices remained at high levels during the first quarter of the year, pushed up by the yen's easing against the dollar, which made oil and gas imports more costly, the federation said.
The utilities review rates on a quarterly basis to reflect fluctuations in fuel procurement costs.
But under government regulations, the utilities are limited to raising their rates by an accumulative total of 1.5 times a base rate set in the July-September period of 1995.
One of the 10 utilities has already hit the maximum, the federation said.
There is no limit on rate cuts.
The federation did not say if the base rate would be changed in the future if the other utilities hit their maximums.
